.NET 10/C# 14 csharparr: put.io/*arr Transmission RPC proxy. Prefer simplicity; avoid over-engineering. Use ASP.NET Core, Serilog, Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience, Tomlyn, xUnit/Moq/FluentAssertions.

PascalCase public; camelCase locals/parameters; _camelCase private; I-prefix interfaces; file-scoped namespaces; records DTOs; nullable enabled; `[]`; `Lock`, not `object`; top-level Program.cs. All I/O-bound operations must be async. Always pass `CancellationToken`; optional parameters use `cancellationToken = default`; suffix async methods `Async`. Catch `OperationCanceledException` separately; log cancellation Debug, not Error. Use `BackgroundService`, bounded `Channel<T>`, cleanup.

Use typed/named HttpClient, IHttpClientFactory, exponential backoff+jitter, circuit breakers, timeouts. Register interfaces and singleton config; test DI/concurrency. Use structured logging. Include HTTP error bodies truncated to 500 chars.

Use Tomlyn; validate all errors at startup. Implement `[Route("/transmission/rpc")]`, `/health` 200, `PropertyNamingPolicy = null`. Multi-stage non-root Dockerfile with HEALTHCHECK. Support linux-x64, linux-arm64, osx-x64, osx-arm64. Tests under `tests/Csharparr.Tests/`.

Don't add features or refactor beyond what's requested
Don't add comments, docstrings, or type annotations to unchanged code
Don't create helpers or abstractions for one-time operations
Don't add error handling for scenarios that can't happen
Don't use `Polly.Extensions.Http` (deprecated)—use `Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience`
Don't log at Error level for expected conditions (cancellation, circuit breaker)
Don't use string interpolation in log messages
Don't register concrete types when interfaces exist
